summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Acme Retail through the Hosted API embeddings and reranking workflow. Focus was on how embeddings + rerank improves search relevance for product search. Discussed candidate generation, index choices, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security considerations (data residency, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a benchmark using Acme's sample data and follow up with pilot pricing and a POC scoping meeting.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme CTO), Priya Rao (Acme ML Eng), Mark Thompson (Acme Search Eng)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account, and Samir is our SE who will run through the demo. How are you all doing?
[00:12] Jordan (Acme): Good thanks, excited to see this. Brief overview — our main goal is to improve product search relevancy and reduce manual tuning. We've tried some vector-based approaches with OpenSearch and Pinecone but results are hit or miss.
[00:27] Samir (Redwood): Great, that's exactly what we'll show — embeddings for semantic recall and then a light-weight rerank stage to surface the best candidates. We'll demo hosted API endpoints and a bit of the Console so you can see metrics.
[00:40] Priya (Acme): Quick question on the scoring — are you doing dot-product or cosine, and is that configurable in the hosted API?
[00:47] Samir (Redwood): Good q. The hosted embeddings endpoint returns dense vectors; similarity can be computed either client-side or via our rerank endpoint which supports dot-product and cosine-based scoring. Config is via a simple param in the rerank call. 
[01:05] Mark (Acme): Also curious about candidate gen — do you expect us to run an ANN index and then call rerank on top-N, or do you offer a candidate generation service?
[01:17] Alex (Redwood): Typical pattern is ANN for fast recall (OpenSearch, FAISS, or managed indexes like Pinecone) then call our rerank endpoint to re-score top-N (we often recommend N between 50-200 depending on latency). We also have suggestions in Redwood Optimize for batching and caching to reduce cost.
[01:35] Jordan: Ok, can you show the actual API calls?

-- Demo starts --
[01:45] Samir: I'll share my screen. (screen share) Starting with the Console — here's the Hosted API quickstart for embeddings, you can see sample cURL and SDK calls. Note: we have models like redwood-emb-1 (demo name) and you can pin versions.
[02:05] Samir: First an embedding call: POST /v1/embeddings with text = "red leather jacket women's". Response returns 1536-d vector (payload truncated in demo). This is what you'd store in your index.
[02:28] Alex: Small aside — the Console shows token-level cost and latency, and Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization or batching if you want to reduce per-token cost.
[02:40] Priya: In your docs you mentioned KV cache, is that used for embeddings or only for generative? I saw a note about KV cash in one doc earlier.
[02:49] Samir: Ha yeah kv cash typo in some autogenerated docs. KV cache is primarily for autoregressive generation. For embeddings rerank flow it's about the index and rerank.
[03:05] Samir: Now the rerank endpoint: POST /v1/rerank with payload including candidates (id + optional text snippet or pre-computed embedding). You can send candidate embeddings to avoid duplicate encoding. The endpoint returns a ranked list and confidence/score for each candidate.
[03:28] Mark: Does rerank recompute embeddings or accept precomputed? Latency difference?
[03:34] Samir: You can send precomputed embeddings for candidates; that keeps rerank very fast because it only does similarity scoring and the light neural scoring head. If you send text for candidates, rerank will embed then score — that adds ~20-50ms per candidate depending on model and sequence length.
[03:55] Jordan: What's a realistic latency for a rerank of 100 candidates in hosted mode?
[04:02] Samir: For 100 candidates with precomputed embeddings, you'll typically see 60-120ms median on our hosted service for the rerank step. If you embed on the fly, add ~150-300ms depending on length. We can provide specific numbers once we run your benchmark.
[04:20] Alex: It's common to do ANN + rerank to keep overall user latency under 200-300ms.

[04:30] Priya: On cost — do you charge separately for embeddings and rerank? How does pricing work?
[04:36] Alex: Yes, embeddings calls are billed per-embedding unit; rerank calls are billed per-request which factors in the number of candidates and model used. We'll send the detailed pricing sheet after this call. We also offer Dedicated for predictable throughput if you want committed capacity.
[04:54] Jordan: For data security, we need SOC2 + KMS + ability to keep logs within region. Is that supported on Hosted?
[05:03] Samir: Hosted supports SOC2 and region selection for data residency in our supported regions. For strict KMS control or air-gapped, Private deployment is the option. But we do support customer-managed KMS integrations for keys in some hosted tiers — I'll flag that to our security docs.
[05:20] Mark: Do you keep raw text or is it ephemeral? We have PII concerns.
[05:25] Samir: By default some logs are retained for debugging but redaction and opt-out settings exist. For pilot we'll propose retention settings and support S3 log exports or no retention depending on the agreement. We'll attach the security whitepaper.

[05:45] Alex: Back to the demo — I want to show a simple end-to-end flow with a small product catalog. Samir, run the example where we query "waterproof hiking jacket".
[05:55] Samir: Running the flow: 1) encode query -> embedding. 2) ANN search against stored embeddings in FAISS (this is a local sim in the demo) -> top 100 candidates. 3) Call rerank with precomputed candidate embeddings -> final ordered list returned.
[06:20] Samir: (shows response) Note the top result here gets a high rerank score, and you can see why in the debug snippet — model pulls up attributes like 'waterproof membrane' and 'taped seams' from the product description.
[06:40] Priya: The debug snippet looks useful. Is that exposed in production? Any PII risk?
[06:47] Samir: Debugging fields are optional and can be turned off; we also mask sensitive fields. Good call to be cautious.

[07:05] Jordan: Regarding evaluation — we have an internal relevance script that computes MRR and NDCG. Will Redwood help run the evals?
[07:13] Alex: Absolutely. We usually run a benchmark as part of the POC. Samir will share a template and we can help run an R script or python notebook to compute MRR/NDCG on your sample.
[07:25] Samir: Also Redwood Optimize can suggest model & quantization parameters per workload. For example, for ecommerce product catalog we often recommend a mid-size emb model plus a small rerank head to balance accuracy/cost.

[07:40] Mark: About index storage — we currently use OpenSearch with an ANN plugin. If we want to keep existing infra, can we use it?
[07:48] Samir: Yes supported. We give recommended config for shard size and distance metric. If you want managed indexes we can plug to a Pinecone-like service. The important part is consistent embedding dims and normalization.
[08:05] Jordan: If we move to Dedicated later, how different is the API?
[08:11] Alex: Same API surface. That's one of our differentiators — same endpoints, different runtime/backing infra. You can pin model versions and rollout policies across environments.

[08:25] Priya: Any known gotchas with rerank and multi-lingual queries? We have localized catalogs.
[08:31] Samir: Model choice matters. Some embedding models support multilingual well; we also recommend per-language embeddings or language detection up front. We can run a quick sample to show performance across locales.

[09:00] (Brief cross talk, small interruptions)

[09:20] Samir: Next I'll demo a sample Python snippet for batch rerank via the SDK: you create candidate array, optionally include embeddings, call client.rerank(candidates=cands, model='redwood-rerank-1', metric='dot'). Response contains scores and ordering.
[09:45] Alex: I'll also point out the Console's logging and per-route dashboards — you can see tail latency and token-level costs. That helps you tune the N and batching policies.

[10:10] Mark: Two practical questions: 1) rate limits for hosted? 2) backoff/retry semantics?
[10:17] Alex: Hosted has soft rate limits based on plan; we'll provide specific TPS numbers in the doc. We support standard 429 handling and exponential backoff patterns; SDKs include helpers.

[10:35] Jordan: Ok let's talk success criteria — what would you consider a successful pilot?
[10:41] Alex: Usually 1) measurable improvement in MRR/NDCG over baseline, 2) acceptable latency under your SLO (e.g., 200-300ms), 3) cost per search within target budget. If those three are met we consider it successful and recommend a phased rollout.

[11:05] Priya: What about A/B testing capabilities? We want to run a canary on 10% of traffic.
[11:12] Samir: Console supports route-based rollouts and canarying. You can route traffic to different model variants and collect metrics, then automatically roll back on regressions.

[11:30] (Longer demo segment walked through code examples and debug output, some pauses and typing sounds)

[22:00] Samir: (after demo) Quick note — the rerank endpoint also supports soft-promote heuristics and custom feature inputs so you can add business signals like stock count or recency into the rerank model.
[22:18] Mark: That's important — we want recency to bump new arrivals.
[22:22] Samir: You can pass numeric feature vectors per candidate and the reranker will incorporate them. We'll provide example payloads.

[25:00] Jordan: I'm thinking about scale — our peak qps 2k searches/sec during sales. How do you recommend handling that?
[25:10] Alex: For that volume you'd want Dedicated or a mixed approach: hosted for steady-state and Dedicated burst/backfill or vice versa. We can size GPUs based on tokens/sec and concurrency, and run load tests during POC.
[25:28] Priya: Do you support SSO and RBAC for the Console?
[25:32] Samir: Yes SSO (SAML/Okta) and role-based access controls are available for enterprise accounts. Audit logs included.

[26:00] (Short tangent discussing procurement timelines)

[28:15] Alex: Let's recap next steps: we'll send pricing, security docs, and a benchmark template. Samir will run the first benchmark once we receive a sample dataset. We'll set a follow-up for POC scoping.
[28:30] Jordan: Sounds good. One more technical ask — can you include a rough estimate of cost per 1M searches with your recommended config?
[28:40] Alex: We'll include a model and infra cost estimate in the proposal; it's approximate until we run the actual benchmark.

[29:00] (Wrap up, small chit chat)
[29:30] Priya: Thanks both, that was super helpful. We'll get the dataset over by Monday.
[29:36] Alex: Great, appreciate it. We'll follow up with all the docs.

[29:45] Meeting end notes (real time stamps inconsistent with duration due to demo pauses and screen-share time)

-- End of transcript --
